title: HeaderDateTime publicly constructable without validation; to_rfc3339/to_timestamp behavior undefined for out-of-range
description:
header_typed.rs:67-124 — HeaderDateTime has 9 public fields, no validation, no documented value ranges:

    pub struct HeaderDateTime {
        pub year: u16,
        pub month: u8,
        pub day: u8,
        pub hour: u8,
        pub minute: u8,
        pub second: u8,
        pub tz_before_gmt: bool,
        pub tz_hour: u8,
        pub tz_minute: u8,
    }

None of the doc comments state the valid range for each field. RFC 5322 §3.3 implies:
  - month ∈ 1..=12
  - day ∈ 1..=31 (calendar-validated against month/year)
  - hour ∈ 0..=23
  - minute ∈ 0..=59
  - second ∈ 0..=59 (RFC 5322 §4.3 allows 60 for leap seconds)
  - tz_hour ∈ 0..=23 (some real-world values exceed; RFC permits up to ±9999)
  - tz_minute ∈ 0..=59

A caller can construct `HeaderDateTime { year: 0, month: 13, day: 99, hour: 25, ... }` and then call `.to_rfc3339()` or `.to_timestamp()`. Behavior is whatever mail-parser does — undocumented from this crate's perspective.

Caller-facing consequence (two-pronged):

a) Direct construction: a JMAP server constructing dates from external sources (database, user input) cannot rely on these methods producing well-formed output. Silently malformed RFC 3339 output is a wire-protocol bug.

b) Mutating after parse: a caller doing `let mut dt = parse_header_typed(...); dt.month = 0;` (e.g., to test a path) can produce an invalid struct from a valid parse. No constructor enforces invariants.

Fix options:
- Add documented ranges to each field doc.
- Add a `HeaderDateTime::new(...) -> Result<Self, _>` validating constructor and make fields pub(crate).
- Document that invalid HeaderDateTime → undefined output from to_rfc3339/to_timestamp.

The cheapest fix is the doc one. Pick a contract and write it down.
close_reason: HeaderDateTime cleanup batch: (.31) tz_before_gmt bool replaced with TzSign enum (East/West); (.9) field invariants documented per field, plus type-level statement that out-of-range values yield unspecified output; (.10) wire-format dependency on mail-parser made explicit with a doc section; (.15) to_rfc3339 doc specifies exact output (Zulu Z for UTC, ±HH:MM otherwise) with examples and out-of-range escape hatch; (.16) to_timestamp doc specifies pre-epoch / out-of-range behaviour. Struct gains #[non_exhaustive]. New test pins Zulu-form output for UTC.
